messages:
maria (arch): thinking out loud — we need a tighter contract between router and runtime for canary warmup + automatic fallback. current behaviour is a bit ad-hoc and causes noisy failovers.
kevin (eng-runtime): +1. curious which gaps you see as highest priority?
sanjay (eng-platform): operationally it's the warmup signals. canaries get traffic before caches/kv are warmed and then error rates spike. triggers the fallback even though runtime would have stabilized.
maria (arch): exactly. propose three primitives: 1) explicit warmup window with probe-oracle, 2) session affinity grace when switching variants, 3) soft-fail escalation rather than hard cutover.
olivia (eng-ml): for model variants we also need a quality gate metric (response divergence) aside from error rate. a canary could be functionally fine but drift in outputs.
kevin (eng-runtime): implementation idea: router negotiates a warmup token with runtime via control plane: "warmup_id" + expected_kv_keys. runtime returns progress updates. router holds back traffic or only sends shadow/readonly traffic until progress >= threshold.
sanjay (eng-platform): love the warmup_id token. that lets us track multiple parallel canaries. suggest adding a TTL for tokens so dead canaries don't block.
maria (arch): agreed. add probing policy defs: probe_interval, success_ratio_threshold, kv_fill_percent. default probe_interval=5s, success_ratio=0.98, kv_fill=60%.
kevin (eng-runtime): sample control plane proto sketch: ```proto
message WarmupClaim {
  string warmup_id = 1;
  repeated string expected_kv_keys = 2;
  int32 kv_target_pct = 3; // 0-100
  double success_ratio = 4;
}
message WarmupStatus {
  string warmup_id = 1;
  double kv_fill_pct = 2;
  double recent_success_ratio = 3;
  bool ready_for_live = 4;
}
```
kevin (eng-runtime): runtime emits WarmupStatus every 5s. router obeys ready_for_live and also can check success_ratio.

oncall (eng-oncall): question: if the runtime never reaches kv_target (e.g., cold dataset), how do we avoid traffic stall?
maria (arch): fallback: after a maximum warmup window (configurable, default 2m) router auto-sends limited live traffic with strict timeouts + circuit monitoring. we treat warmup expiry as "degraded but allowed". also surface a metric that it's in degraded warmup mode.
kevin (eng-runtime): that addresses stalls. we should also support partial-warmup routing: route N% of requests as live, 100% as shadow. N ramps up from 0 to target over time. router can use linear or sigmoid ramps.
sanjay (eng-platform): ops visibility: expose a per-canary dashboard row with warmup_id, kv_fill, success_ratio, live_traffic_pct, fallback_state. this helps SREs avoid blind flips.
olivia (eng-ml): for quality gate: compute token-level BLEU-ish or embedding cosine drift across a reference prompt set. expose "quality_regression_pct". if regression > threshold, auto-fallback.
kevin (eng-runtime): note: embedding cosine checks are heavy; maybe runtime can compute lightweight fingerprints for a small probe set and return scalar drift. platform handles heavier evals asynchronously.
maria (arch): we also need deterministic fallback precedence: prefer degrading QoS (tightening timeouts, smaller token limits), then route to a compatible variant, then route to previous production model, then circuit-break. prioritize non-user-facing degradations first.
oncall (eng-oncall): would be nice if fallback actions emit structured events so runbooks can react automatically.
sanjay (eng-platform): agreed. propose event types: WARMUP_EXPIRED, QUALITY_REGRESSION, ERROR_SURGE, RESOURCE_OVERFLOW. event payload: warmup_id, action_taken, metric_snapshot, trace_link.
maria (arch): interface boundary question: should router decide fallback action locally or ask control plane? pros/cons?
kevin (eng-runtime): local decision gives faster response (ms) but risks divergent policies across routers. control plane centralizes policy, easier auditing and rollback. hybrid approach: fast local heuristics for immediate short-term action, and async control plane reconciliation for longer-term policy enforcement.
olivia (eng-ml): hybrid seems practical. local action can be a short-lived TTL (e.g., 30s) then control plane can confirm or revert.
sanjay (eng-platform): also watch for split-brain: different routers taking different fallbacks for same canary. we need an eviction/lease model: local action wins for TTL but control plane can stamp a canonical state.
maria (arch): corner case: KV cache eviction during ramp — runtime might drop keys and report kv_fill decrease, triggering fallback. suggestion: runtime include a monotonic "warmup_progress_hist" to avoid transient drops causing fallbacks. basically make metrics smoothing mandatory.
kevin (eng-runtime): yes — use EWMA over last N seconds for both kv_fill and success_ratio. we'll publish smoothing window in WarmupStatus.
oncall (eng-oncall): how do we test this safely? can we run a chaos job that simulates cold starts + kv loss?
sanjay (eng-platform): we can create a gated canary test harness: spin up a canary variant, inject synthetic kv empties, induce latency, and assert router respects warmup TTL and fallback tiers. add to our canary e2e tests.
olivia (eng-ml): for canary evals, add small labeled prompt set so we can compute quality_regression quickly. 50 prompts should be enough to detect big regressions.
maria (arch): action items: 1) kevin draft Warmup proto + runtime side EWMA + event hooks, 2) sanjay design router token negotiation + partial-route ramp and dashboard rows, 3) olivia define quick quality probe set + regression calc, 4) me (maria) write short RFC with sequence diagrams and failure modes.
kevin (eng-runtime): will start proto draft today. I'll push to eng-runtime PR and tag you.
sanjay (eng-platform): I'll sketch router state machine and event formats. also propose metrics names: warmup.kv_fill_pct, warmup.success_ratio, warmup.live_pct, warmup.state.
olivia (eng-ml): I'll assemble probe set and a simple embedding-drift scorer we can run on runtime outputs.
oncall (eng-oncall): I'll author a playbook snippet for oncall: how to interpret warmup rows and manual rollback steps.
maria (arch): thanks all. one more: include a compact JSON example for router warmup request so infra folks have something concrete.
sanjay (eng-platform): 
```json
{
  "warmup_id": "canary-2026-03-20-01",
  "expected_kv_keys": ["encoder_vocab", "prefix_cache"],
  "kv_target_pct": 60,
  "success_ratio": 0.98,
  "max_warmup_seconds": 120,
  "ramp_strategy": "linear",
  "ramp_duration_seconds": 60
}
```
kevin (eng-runtime): perfect. also add a runtime hint field: "allow_partial_live": true so router knows it's safe to partial-route.
maria (arch): OK wrapping up. will put RFC draft in docs and @-mention this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary-sim job queued (job_id=87921)
kevin (eng-runtime): :eyes: will watch the job logs and annotate proto PR with findings.
maria (arch): thanks everyone, this is a much cleaner set of primitives than today's heuristics.
oncall (eng-oncall): noted for oncall runbook.
